papers.title: Commutative Algebra Inspired by Modularity Lifting

coverage.read_version: arXiv:2510.11875v2, dated March 31 2026; arXiv revision March 27 2026
coverage.read_pages: All 11 PDF pages: §§1–3 on pp.1–8, acknowledgments and bibliography pp.8–11.
integrated_results: Proposition 2.1 and its depth-chain proof
Theorem 2.2 explicitly restricted to surjective local maps and finite modules
Theorem 2.3 Nagata projective-dimension change
Example 2.4 with explicit Koszul chain homotopy
Question 2.5, Theorem 2.6 including minimal-complex rank formula
Theorem 2.7 explicitly restricted to surjective local maps
Equations (3.1)–(3.6), congruence module, Wiles defect, Fitting/Koszul bridge
Theorems 3.1–3.4, including distinction between a free summand and full freeness
Theorem 3.5 under the explicit sufficient-depth specialization
Proof route of Theorem 3.4 including faithful-image obstruction
Candidate defect module at end of §3, recorded as an open extension problem
full_proofs_integrated: Proposition 2.1, conditional on stated standard depth and regular-local-ring facts
coverage.prerequisite_expansion: Local completion, regular sequences, depth, projective dimension, complete intersections, exceptional surjections, embedding dimension, exterior algebra, DVRs, regular O-valued points, finite length, torsion quotient, MCM modules and Fitting ideals.

deepening.details: Added local algebra proofs and new report branch: homology-action versus derived-action obstruction; Koszul H1 nonfree despite free H0. Original surjective freeness proof investigated and expanded conditionally, not relabelled unconditional.

limitations: No self-contained full proof of Theorems 2.2, 2.3, 2.6, 2.7 or 3.1-3.5 is claimed. The original public proof of the surjective Theorem 2.2 is now expanded relative to Nagata and an annihilator/prime-avoidance input; N=B in Theorem 2.3 is fully proved via Koszul. Basic Nakayama, minimal resolutions, and explicit lifting steps are now fully proved.
The general non-surjective, finite-flat-dimension form of Theorem 2.2 and general-map complete-intersection factorization are not integrated.
Theorem 3.6 on infinitely generated complete big Cohen–Macaulay modules is read but not integrated; derived completion and Gorenstein prerequisites are not developed.
No reconstruction of the number-theoretic modularity lifting arguments, Galois deformation theory, patching, or R=T proofs.
The candidate defect module has no claimed unconditional vanishing or length theorem.

papers.title: The Taming of 3-fold Flops

coverage.read_version: SIAM published version, also deposited as Published Version in University of Glasgow Enlighten 390795
coverage.read_pages: All 13 PDF pages: body pp.305–314 (§§1.1–1.9 and §§2.1–2.3.2), bibliography pp.315–317.
visual_checks: PDF p.314: equation (2.3), Lemma 2.5 and its nonzero-cohomology footnote
PDF p.315: bibliography marks [11] and [12] in preparation
integrated_results: §1.3 stable-endomorphism construction of the contraction algebra
Theorem 1.3 August derived-class closure for basic algebras
Theorem 1.4 Donovan–Wemyss reconstruction, with complete-local/smooth hypotheses
Single-curve specialization from derived equivalence to algebra isomorphism
Theorem 1.5(1) and 1.5(2) kept as separate statements
§2.3.2 unitally positive A-infinity subalgebra, Lemma 2.5 and an expanded degree proof
§2.3.2 reconstruction route with the geometric inputs explicitly marked as unproved inputs
Tjurina algebra and fixed-dimensional characteristic-zero isolated-hypersurface reconstruction background
§1.5 cyclic derivatives and Jacobi algebras, including explicit A-type and noncommutative computations
§1.6 gluing equation (1.3) and only the first family of Theorem 1.7
full_proofs_integrated: Lemma 2.5 degree argument, conditional on the stated strictly-unital minimal-model theorem
coverage.prerequisite_expansion: ADE/cDV complete-local equations, projectivity, smooth small local contractions, coherent sheaves, tilting bundles, stable endomorphisms, basic algebras, derived equivalence, DG quasi-isomorphisms, derived endomorphisms, minimal A-infinity structures and derived quotients.

deepening.details: Added explicit derived quotient low cohomology, full two-cycle DG calculation, and odd-exponent Laufer Jacobi/abelianization calculations. Geometry and homotopy-universal identification are separate inputs.

limitations: The full six-family normal-form classification, algebraic length, ADE preprojective corner algebras, and Theorem 1.8 are read but not encoded as a complete classification dataset.
Theorem 1.6, Theorem 1.7 and Theorem 2.3 refer to [11]/[12] marked in preparation in this exact report; their complete proofs were not publicly supplied by this report and are not claimed read.
Only Theorem 1.7's first/A-type family is integrated, with explicit status metadata; no assertion that arbitrary gluing data contract.
The unique-enhancement/derived Auslander–Iyama route of §2.3.1 is read but not fully formalized; its hypotheses are not silently dropped into an unconditional theorem.

GV/Toda numerical invariants, noncommutative deformation representability, cluster-tilting correspondence, singular terminal-flop extensions, and wider applications remain unproved or undeveloped. Concrete Laufer algebra/abelianization dimensions are now proved, but not their geometric deformation interpretation.
The reconstruction route distinguishes the special geometric identification from mere injectivity on cohomology; no general DG algebra is claimed determined by H0.
